1→# gmeta POC Plan
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→gmeta is a proposed standard for attaching arbitrary metadata to Git projects, designed by Scott Chacon (GitButler). It defines a tree layout spec for serializing `(target, key, value)` tuples into Git trees on `refs/meta/local/main`, exchangeable over standard Git protocol.
     6→
     7→Entire's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is functionally equivalent to jj's `change-id` — a stable identifier embedded in the commit message that survives rebase/cherry-pick. This maps directly to gmeta's `change-id` target type, meaning checkpoint metadata keyed to `change-id:<checkpoint-id>` survives rewrites without any additional tooling.
     8→
     9→Reference implementation: `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta`
    10→Spec: `gmeta/spec/README.md`
    11→
    12→## Goal
    13→
    14→Write Entire checkpoint metadata in gmeta exchange format alongside v1/v2, proving interop by reading it back with the Rust `gmeta` CLI.
    15→
    16→## Architecture
    17→
    18→No go-git changes needed. gmeta is just a tree layout convention — Entire already has all the plumbing:
    19→- `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit` in `checkpoint/`
    20→- `V2GitStore` as prior art for a second store struct composing `GitStore`
    21→- Dual-write pattern already exists in `manual_commit_condensation.go`
    22→
    23→## Tree Layout Mapping
    24→
    25→### Fanout Rule
    26→
    27→Per gmeta spec (`spec/exchange-format/exchange.md`), `change-id` targets use: **first 2 hex chars of SHA-1(target-value)**.
    28→
    29→So for checkpoint ID `a3b2c4d5e6f7`: fanout = `sha1("a3b2c4d5e6f7")[:2]`.
    30→
    31→This is NOT the same as `checkpoint-id[:2]`. The fanout is derived from a hash of the value, not the value itself.
    32→
    33→### Per-Session Encoding
    34→
    35→A checkpoint can contain multiple sessions (concurrent agents, `entire attach`). gmeta has no native session concept, so we namespace per session under the checkpoint's change-id target:
    36→
    37→```
    38→change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
    39→├── entire/
    40→│   ├── strategy/__value                           # "manual-commit"
    41→│   ├── cli-version/__value                        # CLI version
    42→│   ├── branch/__value                             # branch name
    43→│   ├── checkpoints-count/__value                  # total across all sessions
    44→│   └── files-touched/__set/                       # merged from all sessions
    45→│       ├── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/foo.go"
    46→│       └── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/bar.go"
    47→├── session/
    48→│   ├── ids/__list/                                # ordered session IDs
    49→│   │   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid1"
    50→│   │   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid2"
    51→│   ├── <session-id-1>/
    52→│   │   ├── agent/
    53→│   │   │   ├── name/__value                       # "Claude Code"
    54→│   │   │   ├── model/__value                      # "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"
    55→│   │   │   └── provider/__value                   # "anthropic"
    56→│   │   ├── prompt/__value                         # user prompt(s)
    57→│   │   └── transcript/__list/                     # chunked JSONL entries
    58→│   │       ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
    59→│   │       └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
    60→│   └── <session-id-2>/
    61→│       ├── agent/
    62→│       │   ├── name/__value
    63→│       │   ├── model/__value
    64→│       │   └── provider/__value
    65→│       ├── prompt/__value
    66→│       └── transcript/__list/
    67→│           └── ...
    68→```
    69→
    70→This means:
    71→- Checkpoint-level fields (`strategy`, `branch`, `files-touched`) live at the top level
    72→- Each session gets its own subtree under `session/<session-id>/`
    73→- `session/ids` is a list preserving session ordering
    74→- Adding a session (via `entire attach` or concurrent agent) appends to `session/ids` and creates a new `session/<id>/` subtree — no overwrites
    75→
    76→### Single-Session Shorthand
    77→
    78→When there is exactly one session, the layout is identical — just one `session/<id>/` subtree. No special-casing needed.
    79→
    80→## Security: Redaction
    81→
    82→All data written to `refs/meta/local/main` MUST be redacted before creating git blobs, matching v1/v2 behavior:
    83→
    84→- Transcripts: pass through `redact.JSONLBytes()` before chunking into list entries
    85→- Prompts: pass through `redact.String()` before writing `__value` blob
    86→- File paths in `files-touched`: no redaction needed (already public via git history)
    87→
    88→This is a hard requirement, not an implementation detail. The gmeta ref is permanent and pushable.
    89→
    90→## Write Paths
    91→
    92→`GmetaStore` must be wired into **all** paths that write committed checkpoints, not just condensation:
    93→
    94→| Write path | File | When | Task checkpoints |
    95→|---|---|---|---|
    96→| Condensation | `manual_commit_condensation.go` | PostCommit hook — session data condensed on user commit | Full support |
    97→| Stop finalization | `manual_commit_hooks.go` | Stop hook — transcript/prompts replaced with final versions | Full support |
    98→| Attach | `attach.go` | `entire attach` — adds external session data to existing checkpoint | Full support |
    99→| Migrate | `migrate.go` | `entire migrate` — copies v1 checkpoints to v2 (and now gmeta) | **Session data only** |
   100→
   101→**Migrate and task checkpoints**: Migration copies task metadata from v1 to v2 via raw tree splicing (`copyTaskMetadataToV2`), not through `WriteCommittedOptions` — the opts only carry `IsTask` and `ToolUseID`, not `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, subagent transcript content, or incremental payloads. Building a v1-tree-walker that re-extracts all task fields into gmeta format is not worth the complexity for a one-time operation. The gmeta migrate path writes session-level data only; task metadata remains available in v1 and v2.
   102→
   103→### Task Checkpoint Encoding
   104→
   105→Task checkpoints (subagent work) are written under `session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`:
   106→
   107→```
   108→session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/
   109→├── agent-id/__value                              # subagent identifier (opts.AgentID)
   110→├── checkpoint-uuid/__value                       # UUID for transcript truncation on rewind (opts.CheckpointUUID)
   111→├── transcript/__list/                            # subagent transcript (chunked, from opts.SubagentTranscriptPath)
   112→│   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
   113→│   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
   114→└── incremental/__list/                           # incremental checkpoints (ordered)
   115→    ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                       # JSON: {type, tool_use_id, data}
   116→    └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
   117→```
   118→
   119→These fields map 1:1 to what `WriteCommittedOptions` already carries: `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, `SubagentTranscriptPath`, and `IncrementalData`/`IncrementalType`/`IncrementalSequence`. No new plumbing needed.
   120→
   121→**Final task checkpoints** write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, and `transcript` entries.
   122→
   123→**Incremental task checkpoints** (`opts.IsIncremental`) append to `incremental/__list/`. Each entry is a JSON blob with `{type, tool_use_id, timestamp, data}` — same content as v1's `checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json` but as a gmeta list entry instead of numbered files.
   124→
   125→Redaction applies to both: subagent transcripts via `redact.JSONLBytes()` (falling back to `redact.Bytes()`), incremental data via `redact.JSONLBytes()`.
   126→
   127→### Write API
   128→
   129→```go
   130→type GmetaStore struct {
   131→    repo *git.Repository
   132→    gs   *GitStore
   133→}
   134→
   135→// WriteCommitted writes or appends a session to a checkpoint in gmeta format.
   136→// If the checkpoint already exists, the new session is added alongside existing ones.
   137→// Handles both session and task checkpoints (including incremental).
   138→func (s *GmetaStore) WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error
   139→
   140→// UpdateCommitted replaces transcript and prompts for an existing session.
   141→// Used at stop time to finalize with complete session data.
   142→// Replaces the transcript list entries and prompt value for the given session.
   143→func (s *GmetaStore) UpdateCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts UpdateCommittedOptions) error
   144→```
   145→
   146→Both methods required from day one. `UpdateCommitted` replaces the `session/<id>/transcript/__list/` entries and `session/<id>/prompt/__value` blob for the target session. This matches the replace semantics v1/v2 already use — gmeta lists are append-only in the *exchange* model, but within a single serialization we control the full tree, so replacing entries before push is fine.
   147→
   148→### Wiring Pattern
   149→
   150→Same as v2 — non-fatal wrapper so gmeta failures don't break existing flow:
   151→
   152→```go
   153→gmetaStore := cpkg.NewGmetaStore(repo)
   154→if err := gmetaStore.WriteCommitted(ctx, opts); err != nil {
   155→    logging.Warn(ctx, "gmeta write failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   156→}
   157→```
   158→
   159→Applied in all four write paths above.
   160→
   161→## Steps
   162→
   163→### Step 1: GmetaStore struct + WriteCommitted + UpdateCommitted
   164→
   165→New file: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go`
   166→
   167→Implementation details:
   168→- String values: blob at `<key-path>/__value`
   169→- List values: blobs at `<key-path>/__list/<timestamp-ms>-<hash5>`
   170→- Set values: blobs at `<key-path>/__set/<sha1-of-value[:10]>` containing the value
   171→- Target base path: `change-id/<sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]>/<checkpoint-id>/`
   172→- Ref: `refs/meta/local/main`
   173→- Redaction: `redact.JSONLBytes()` for transcripts, `redact.String()` for prompts
   174→- Multi-session: read existing tree, find/create `session/<id>/` subtree
   175→
   176→Reuses from `GitStore`: `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit`
   177→
   178→### Step 2: Wire into all write paths
   179→
   180→Add `GmetaStore` calls to condensation, stop finalization, attach, and migrate. Non-fatal in all paths.
   181→
   182→### Step 3: Validate interop
   183→
   184→Install the Rust gmeta CLI, point at a repo with Entire checkpoints:
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:agent:model
   188→gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:prompt
   189→gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:transcript
   190→gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> entire:files-touched
   191→```
   192→
   193→Verify data round-trips correctly.
   194→
   195→## Open Questions
   196→
   197→- **Token usage / attribution**: Entire-specific structured data. Options:
   198→  - Namespace as individual keys: `session/<id>/entire:token-usage:input/__value`, etc.
   199→  - Or store as JSON string under `session/<id>/entire:token-usage/__value`
   200→  - Decision: defer to after POC, not needed for interop validation
   201→- **Push/fetch**: gmeta uses `refs/meta/local/main` for push, `refs/meta/remotes/main` for fetch. Need to decide if this coexists with or replaces v2's push mechanism. Likely coexists for now.
   202→- **Read-side**: Not needed for POC. Future work to have `entire session list/show` read from gmeta format.
   203→- **Task checkpoints**: Included. Final tasks write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, `transcript` under `session/<id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`. Incremental tasks append to `incremental/__list/`. Open question: should the gmeta Rust CLI understand these Entire-specific task keys, or are they opaque vendor-namespaced data?
   204→
   205→## Estimated Scope
   206→
   207→~300-400 lines for `GmetaStore` (write + update + multi-session handling + redaction), ~20 lines to wire into all four write paths. Tests + interop validation on top.

1→# Serialization
     2→
     3→This document describes how to serialize metadata into Git primatives that can be transferred via normal Git remote protocols.
     4→
     5→[Interactive demo of the serialization format](../other/example-serialize.html)
     6→
     7→## Commit model
     8→
     9→Serialization writes a Git commit whose tree contains the current shareable metadata state.
    10→
    11→- tree pointer
    12→- author identity
    13→- author date / commit date
    14→- ancestry for incremental materialization and merging
    15→
    16→## Tree root layout
    17→
    18→The base tree path for a target is target-type dependent:
    19→
    20→- `commit` → `<target-type>/<first2-of-sha>/<full-target-value>`
    21→- `branch` / `change-id` → `<target-type>/<fanout>/<full-target-value>`
    22→- `path` → `path/<escaped path segments...>/__target__`
    23→- `project` → `project`
    24→
    25→Fanout is target-type dependent:
    26→
    27→- for `commit`, use the first 2 characters of the commit SHA
    28→- for `path`, do not hash the target value; serialize the path segments directly
    29→- for anything else (`branch`, `change-id`), use the first 2 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-1 hash of the target value (ie, the branch name or change-id value)
    30→
    31→Examples:
    32→
    33→- `commit/13/13a7d29cde8f8557b54fd6474f547a56822180ae/...`
    34→- `branch/06/sc-branch-1-deadbeef/...`
    35→- `path/src/metrics/__target__/owner/__value`
    36→
    37→For `path` targets, a reserved separator component `__target__` marks the end of the target path and the beginning of key segments.
    38→If a serialized path segment would begin with `__`, it must be escaped by prefixing it with `~`.
    39→To keep this reversible, a path segment beginning with `~` should also be escaped by prefixing it with `~`.
    40→Examples:
    41→
    42→- raw path segment `__generated` → serialized as `~__generated`
    43→- raw path segment `~scratch` → serialized as `~~scratch`
    44→
    45→This keeps commit paths readable, preserves human-readable path targets, and still avoids ambiguity between serialized path targets and metadata structure.
    46→
    47→## Key path layout
    48→
    49→Under the target base path, key segments are serialized directly as path components.
    50→
    51→Metadata structure begins when a reserved `__*` component is encountered.
    52→
    53→Examples:
    54→
    55→- string: `<base>/agent/model/__value`
    56→- list: `<base>/agent/chat/__list/<entry-id>`
    57→- whole-key tombstone: `<base>/__tombstones/agent/model/__deleted`
    58→
    59→## Per-type layouts
    60→
    61→Per-type layouts are defined in:
    62→
    63→- [Strings](./strings.md)
    64→- [Lists](./lists.md)
    65→- [Sets](./sets.md)
    66→
    67→## Key path reservation
    68→
    69→Keys are serialized directly under the target base path.
    70→
    71→Any path component beginning with `__` is reserved for gmeta structural paths such as:
    72→
    73→- `__value`
    74→- `__list`
    75→- `__set`
    76→- `__tombstones`
    77→- `__target__` (used only as the separator inside serialized `path` targets)
    78→
    79→This means user keys occupy normal path segments and metadata structure begins when a reserved `__*` path component is encountered.
    80→
    81→## Path target encoding
    82→
    83→`path` targets are serialized using their raw path segments rather than a hash-derived fanout prefix.
    84→
    85→Shape:
    86→
    87→`path/<escaped path segments...>/__target__/...`
    88→
    89→Rules:
    90→
    91→- each `/`-separated path component becomes one tree path component
    92→- `__target__` marks the end of the target path and the beginning of key segments
    93→- if a path segment begins with `__`, escape it by prefixing the segment with `~`
    94→- if a path segment begins with `~`, also escape it by prefixing the segment with `~`
    95→
    96→Examples:
    97→
    98→- `path:src/metrics` → `path/src/metrics/__target__/...`
    99→- `path:src/__generated/file.rs` → `path/src/~__generated/file.rs/__target__/...`
   100→- `path:src/~scratch/file.rs` → `path/src/~~scratch/file.rs/__target__/...`
   101→
   102→## Explicit deletion
   103→
   104→Exchange must not assume that missing paths mean deletion.
   105→
   106→Reasons:
   107→
   108→- sparse or pruned trees may omit data
   109→- multiple metadata refs may represent different subsets
   110→- absence should not be ambiguous
   111→
   112→Intentional deletion is represented by explicit tombstones.
   113→
   114→A single reserved `__tombstones` namespace is used for both whole-key and child-level deletions. Child tombstones are interpreted relative to the current key type. Serialize and materialize must ignore incompatible child tombstones for the current type rather than treating them as errors or as deletions for another collection model.

1→# Strings
     2→
     3→Strings are the simplest gmeta value type.
     4→
     5→A string represents one current scalar value for a `(target, key)` pair.
     6→
     7→Examples:
     8→
     9→- `agent:model = claude-4.6`
    10→- `owner = schacon`
    11→- `review:signoff = schacon@gmail.com`
    12→
    13→## Summary
    14→
    15→- One current value per key
    16→- Serialized as a single terminal blob
    17→- Removal uses a key tombstone
    18→- Concurrent updates resolve by last-writer-wins
    19→
    20→## Serialized tree shape
    21→
    22→For a string value, write the string to:
    23→
    24→`[base]/<key segments>/__value`
    25→
    26→Examples:
    27→
    28→- `commit/13/<full-target>/agent/model/__value`
    29→- `path/src/metrics/__target__/owner/__value`
    30→
    31→The blob contents are the raw string value.
    32→
    33→## Tombstones
    34→
    35→If a string key is removed, serialize a tombstone at:
    36→
    37→`[base]/__tombstones/<key segments>/__deleted`
    38→
    39→The tombstone blob should be the same blob as the `__value` was. This way Git reuses the blob and we can do content comparisons if needed in cases of conflict.
    40→
    41→When a string is set again after deletion, the tombstone is cleared locally and omitted from the next serialization.
    42→
    43→## Merge semantics
    44→
    45→Merging trees can technically use either `ours` or `theirs` strategies, but one value should win out. Projects or individuals can determine which they prefer.
    46→
    47→The default in our implementation is `ours`, so that both values are in the history and reverting is possible.

1→# Lists
     2→
     3→Lists in gmeta are append-friendly multi-value collections.
     4→
     5→They are best thought of as an ordered append log of string entries, not as a general-purpose mutable array.
     6→
     7→Examples:
     8→
     9→- agent transcript jsonl chunks
    10→- review comments
    11→- a sequence of notes appended over time
    12→
    13→## Intended semantics
    14→
    15→The current list design is optimized for the most common concurrent operation: one or more users append new values to the same logical list.
    16→
    17→We serialize lists as many small blobs rather than one JSON array blob so we can use normal Git tree merging tooling to avoid array-level conflicts.
    18→
    19→## Serialized tree shape
    20→
    21→For a list value, entries are written under:
    22→
    23→`[base]/<key segments>/__list/<entry-id>`
    24→
    25→Where `<entry-id>` is of the form:
    26→
    27→`<timestamp-ms>-<content-hash-prefix>`
    28→
    29→Examples:
    30→
    31→- `branch/06/sc-branch-1-deadbeef/agent/chat/__list/1771232450203-23c0f`
    32→- `path/src/metrics/__target__/comments/__list/1771232450203-23c0f`
    33→
    34→Each blob contains one string entry.
    35→
    36→If multiple values are inserted in one command, start from one base millisecond timestamp and increment by 1 for each additional entry so local order is preserved.
    37→
    38→## Ordering
    39→
    40→List order is defined by sorting `<entry-id>` lexically, which is equivalent to sorting by:
    41→
    42→1. timestamp ascending
    43→2. hash suffix as a stable tie-breaker
    44→
    45→This gives deterministic ordering after merges.
    46→
    47→## Duplicate values
    48→
    49→Lists allow duplicate string values.
    50→
    51→If the same text is appended twice at different times, both entries remain.
    52→
    53→This is intentional and differentiates lists from sets.
    54→

    56→

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface{ BlobObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error); TreeObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error) }, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			_, _ = reader.Read(content)
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}
